title: Hedged reconnect protocol and partial draft snapshot pruning
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Clients disconnect or observe long-tail stalls during streaming generations (esp. function-call flows). Partial generations pile up in the prefix-KV cache and ephemeral snapshots, causing increased memory pressure, non-idempotent tool invocations on reconnect, and unpredictable client UX.

Goal: Implement a hedged-reconnect protocol plus a deterministic partial-draft snapshot pruning strategy to (1) reduce perceived stall latency for clients by hedging reconnect attempts, (2) bound memory and KV cache growth from abandoned partial generations through TTL/compaction, and (3) ensure tool/function calls remain idempotent and not re-issued on reconnection races.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace global session GC policy, nor does it change long-term retention for audited output stored for compliance. It also does not implement cross-region routing fallbacks (separate RFC).
acceptance_criteria: Hedged reconnect attempts are gated by per-session lease tokens and cause no duplicate tool invocations (verified via e2e test harness).
Partial-draft snapshots have a compaction policy that reclaims >90% of abandoned snapshots older than 10 minutes in the synthetic load test while preserving resume success for active clients.
Metrics emitted: reconnect_latency_p50/p95/p99, hedged_reconnect_count, snapshot_prune_rate, duplicate_tool_invocation_count; dashboards added to Console.
Rollout plan executed with canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and rollback target of 15 minutes if duplicate_tool_invocation_count > 1/min above baseline.
implementation_notes: Hedged reconnect model: on client-detected stall (idle > X ms or explicit client reconnect), start a secondary reconnect attempt after HedgeDelay (default 120ms) to a hot-standby runtime shard; both attempts race to resume. The first successful resume wins; others are cancelled via lease tombstones.

Lease tokens: generation lease is renewed on successful resume; reconnect attempts must present the current lease token. A short-lived epoch tombstone prevents dual-active resumes. See lease epoch semantics in ENG-58321 for compatibility.

Snapshot pruning: keep partial-draft snapshots in 'warm' KV namespace with tiered TTLs: recent (<1m)=preserve, mid (1m-10m)=compact (strip intermediate deltas), old (>10m)=prune. Compaction reduces memory footprint and retains a resume prefix if available.

Tool-call idempotency: every outbound tool/function invocation during streaming includes an idempotency token derived from session_id + sequence_number + snapshot_hash. On reconnect, runtime checks token store before invoking. Idempotency store is bounded and uses LRU with TTL aligned to snapshot TTL.

Backpressure interaction: hedged reconnect must respect server-side concurrency tokens. Hedged attempts cost an extra concurrency slot; the runtime will rate-limit hedged attempts per customer tier to avoid overload.

Compatibility: Ensure the protocol works with structured-output streaming (jsonl tool sequences) and with older SDKs that lack explicit reconnect hedging by falling back to single reconnect path. Implement a compatibility header 'X-RW-Hedge=1' in the resume handshake.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease token state machine, token collision scenarios, and idempotency token checks.
Integration tests: simulate client disconnects mid-function-call with both hedged and non-hedged clients; assert no duplicate tool invocations and successful resume when possible.
Load test: 1000 concurrent streaming sessions, inject random disconnects and stalls; verify snapshot prune reduces memory growth to below baseline+10%.
Chaos test: delayed reconnect responses and network partitions to validate tombstone expiration and fallback behavior.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'hedged_reconnect' default off. Enable for 5% of traffic in canary pool for 72h.
Monitor duplicate_tool_invocation_count and reconnect_latency metrics. If duplicate invocations spike >1/min above baseline during canary, roll back flag immediately.
Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with 48h observation windows, run full regression on Dedicated capacity customers before 100%.
Post-rollout: add autotune to HedgeDelay based on observed p99 stall durations.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after post-mortem on customer incident where long-tail stall caused duplicate tool calls and memory pressure. Captured initial goals and API compatibility constraints.

2025-02-14 - Benji Morales: Design sync with runtime and SDK leads. Decided on lease-epoch tombstone and idempotency token pattern. Action: Benji to prototype token store in runtime and add compatibility header.

2025-02-16 - Implementation update: prototype hedged reconnect implemented in runtime core; local integration shows 40ms median stall reduction under synthetic workload. Observed edge-case where tombstone expiration caused a 200ms resume regression — adjusting tombstone TTL heuristics.
2025-02-18 - QA: Integration tests added to CI; running chaos suite tonight. Noted flakiness in delayed tool response scenario; creating follow-up sub-issue for tool-call retry semantics.
notes: Follow-up ticket recommended to integrate hedged metrics into Console alerting templates.
Coordinate with Dedicated capacity SRE to ensure hedged reconnects do not starve reserved slots during peak windows.
Keep UX-consistency: client SDKs should expose a single 'resume' API; hedging handled transparently by runtime unless SDK opts out.
